title: Microeconomic reform
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest point, supply-side policies, is broader and covers state-led measures too, while microeconomic reform is a narrower, market-focused subset of it, so no existing point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Microeconomic reform
card: Microeconomic reform is a set of policies that change how particular industries and markets work. The aim is to make them more efficient and more productive.
Efficient means using resources with little waste. Productive means getting more output from the same inputs of labour, land and capital.
Reform often works by exposing firms to more competition or removing rules that hold them back. Firms then have a stronger reason to cut costs and improve.

Gains across many industries can lift the economy's productive capacity over the long term. This supports growth with lower inflationary pressure. It is a supply-side approach, not a way to change spending in the short term.
draft.remember: Microeconomic reform targets how industries work, to lift long-term productive capacity.

a.q: What is the main aim of microeconomic reform?
opts: Make industries more efficient and productive
Change total spending to smooth the business cycle
Raise the price level to help firms earn more
Move the exchange rate to lift export sales
a.why: Microeconomic reform changes how industries and markets work so they use resources better. The option about total spending describes short-term demand management, which is a different kind of policy.
a.clue: Think about industries and markets, not the whole economy's spending.

b.q: A government removes a rule that stops new firms from entering the taxi industry. Prices fall and firms improve their service. Why is this an example of microeconomic reform?
opts: It changes how one market works to raise efficiency
It cuts total spending to slow the whole economy
It changes interest rates to affect borrowing
It changes the budget to offset the business cycle
b.why: Removing the entry rule changes how a single market works, and competition pushes firms to cut costs and improve. The spending option is wrong because the policy targets one industry, not total demand in the short term.
b.clue: Look at the size of the change: one market or the whole economy?

a.best: Make industries more efficient and productive

b.best: It changes how one market works to raise efficiency
